tasks.title: sim: scenario generator v0 emitting valid scenario files
tasks.goal: A seeded kitchen simulator (bins with profiles, plating spot, wash, clean stack, pass, 1-3 cooks, tools, tickets) in kitchen/sim/kitchen.py and scenarios.py that runs simple prep workflows and writes scenario files whose expected answers come from the simulated world, not from any propagation engine.
acceptance: uv run python -m kitchen.sim.scenarios generate --seed 7 --count 5 --out data/scenarios/ writes 5 files that validate against scenario.schema.json: test_generated_valid
The same (generator version, seed) produces byte-identical files: test_deterministic
Ground truth comes from sampled true transfers and washes; expected.decision is hold iff a forbidden unit truly reached the plate: test_truth_from_world
Fresh plates come from a clean_stack zone (late_entities origin clean_stack); every scenario carries tag generated, plus observation-complete when every true transfer was emitted: test_tags
No import from kitchen.graph or kitchen.verdict anywhere in kitchen/sim except verdict's published LayaClient fakes: test_no_forbidden_imports
uv run pytest kitchen/sim passes; kitchen/sim/README.md documents the v0 world model and CLI
out_of_scope: Error injection beyond a single happy-path workflow (sim-06)

tasks.title: sim: ADR for ground-truth and observation model
tasks.goal: Decide and document how the simulated world moves allergens and how observations are derived from it, so sim's answers stay independent of the partner's graph and the verdict policy.
acceptance: Team ADR PR to docs/decisions/ (Director merges) covering per-action true transfer rates, wash efficacy, observation noise on probability, dropped edges, and track loss -> late_entities with origin unknown
Defines hard vs soft expectations: for generated scenarios an expected hold is a hard requirement and an expected pass is a target; only observation-complete scenarios gate CI
Flags the gap that scenario.schema.json expresses these semantics only through tags, and proposes an RFC if a field is needed

tasks.title: sim: M0 corpus of >= 20 scenarios and CI subset
tasks.goal: Produce the M0 exit corpus covering the basic shapes every consumer needs.
acceptance: >= 20 generated scenarios covering basic transfer, wash reset, time order, multi-cook, shared utensil, a clean-stack plate and a ticket with two constraints, listed in a manifest with sha256: test_manifest_matches
A CI subset <= 200 KB committed under kitchen/sim/tests/fixtures/scenarios/; the full set regenerates from seeds: uv run python -m kitchen.sim.scenarios generate --manifest kitchen/sim/corpus-m0.json
Every file passes the same checks as tools/validate_contracts.py (schema, unique event IDs, bindings, chain references, wash self-loops): uv run pytest kitchen/sim -k corpus_valid

tasks.title: sim: propose three edge-case golden scenarios
tasks.goal: Hand-write golden scenarios for edges the first six don't cover, as a contract-change PR the Director merges.
acceptance: Three new files in contracts/scenarios/: equal or overlapping timestamps (expected decision under the strict tie default in OQ-17), a two-hop transfer through a hand, and a double wash; each description explains why the expected decision holds for any k in (0, 1]
python3 tools/validate_contracts.py passes
PR labeled contract-change, linked from a type:rfc issue with ACKs from verdict and platform and a note to the partner (owner:partner), since the graph must pass them too

tasks.title: sim: export scenarios as event and entity JSONL
tasks.goal: Turn any scenario into the replay streams other teams consume: interaction_event JSONL and an entity timeline JSONL.
acceptance: uv run python -m kitchen.sim.scenarios export --scenario <file> --out <dir> writes events.jsonl (one interaction_event per line, time-ordered) and entities.jsonl (one entity per line, with origin): test_export_valid
Every line validates against its schema: test_lines_valid
Round trip scenario -> JSONL -> scenario preserves events exactly: test_round_trip

tasks.title: sim: error-injection library
tasks.goal: Composable injectors in kitchen/sim/errors.py for the mistakes and sensing failures that matter, each changing the simulated world or the observation model, never the expected answer directly.
acceptance: Injectors skipped_wash, shared_utensil, bare_hand_contact, late_entity, track_loss (re-ID as a new entity in late_entities with origin unknown), amendment, dropped_edge and probability_noise, each unit-tested: uv run pytest kitchen/sim -k inject
dropped_edge removes the observation-complete tag; the others keep it: test_tag_semantics
Injectors compose under one seed and stay deterministic: test_compose_deterministic

tasks.title: sim: 500-scenario corpus, CI subset and metrics script
tasks.goal: A large corpus outside git, a committed observation-complete CI subset that verdict gates on, and a script that scores any verdict stream against it.
acceptance: >= 500 scenarios generated to data/ with data-manifest.json (name, size, sha256, generator version, seeds)
Committed CI subset <= 1 MB of observation-complete scenarios spanning every injector except dropped_edge
uv run python -m kitchen.sim.scenarios metrics --scenarios <dir> --verdicts <verdicts.jsonl> prints false-pass count, false-hold rate and a per-tag breakdown: test_metrics_counts

tasks.title: sim: Laya dataset generator v0 with leak-free splits
tasks.goal: Build (laya_request, target laya_response) pairs from simulated plate subgraphs, with ground-truth allergens and true chains, split so test data never leaks into training.
acceptance: uv run python -m kitchen.sim.laya_data --corpus <dir> --out data/laya/ writes train/val/test JSONL; every request and response validates: test_pairs_valid
Splits by seed range AND held-out kitchen/recipe families; a test fails if any seed or scenario_id appears in two splits: test_no_leakage
Manifest with counts and sha256 per split
out_of_scope: Prompt or format design for a specific model

tasks.title: sim: model-agnostic Laya eval harness v0
tasks.goal: Evaluate any LayaClient on the test split, with the gate that Laya never misses an allergen the reference finds. The reference is ground truth today and ExactLaya on the partner's real graph once it lands. Uses verdict's published ExactLaya and AdversarialLaya fakes through LayaClient once they exist.
acceptance: uv run python -m kitchen.sim.laya_eval --client <import path> --split test writes report.json and report.md
Reports recall vs reference (gate: 100%), precision and recall vs ground truth, chain correctness, latency p50/p95, malformed rate: test_report_fields
Exits non-zero when the gate fails: a client that drops allergens fails it and a ground-truth client passes it: test_gate_behaviour
Final step (needs-partner): --reference exact runs ExactLaya over the partner's graph and the gate still behaves the same

tasks.title: sim: StateClient load generator
tasks.goal: Replay a long scenario through any StateClient at target rates and report throughput and latency, so the partner can verify the database's budget.
acceptance: uv run python -m kitchen.sim.scenarios load --client <import path> --profile default drives upsert_entities at 5 Hz x 30 entities and record_interactions bursts up to 20/s
Reports p50/p95/p99 call latency and error counts as JSON
Runs against InMemoryStateClient in CI with a short profile: test_load_inmemory
Final step (needs-partner): run against the partner's real StateClient on a local SpacetimeDB and post the report on an issue labeled owner:partner

tasks.title: sim: long-shift stress scenario
tasks.goal: An 8-hour simulated shift with thousands of edges and many plates, kept outside git, for the partner graph's and verdict's performance budgets.
acceptance: uv run python -m kitchen.sim.scenarios generate --profile long-shift --seed 1 produces a valid scenario with >= 5,000 events and >= 100 plates
Listed in data-manifest.json with sha256; regenerates byte-identically
Generation finishes in under 2 minutes on a laptop, reported in the PR
out_of_scope: Running the graph or verdict on it

tasks.title: sim: ADR for the 2D clip renderer (with partner review)
tasks.goal: Decide how the simulated world becomes ConvLSTM training clips: abstract rendering (no realistic utensils), how food moves and smears on contact, what contact and transferred mean, the hard negatives and their share, domain randomization, and how sim masks are calibrated against real ones.
acceptance: ADR PR in docs/decisions/ (Director merges) covering: world kinematics in 2D; abstract RGB rendering (randomized textures, colors, sizes, plain tool shapes, food blobs); the material motion model; label definitions for contact, transferred, action, direction and contact_t_ms; the hard-negative list with target shares; domain randomization ranges; noise and flicker models; frame-timing jitter
States that clips are built only through kitchen/shared/change_mask.py and clips.py, and that labels come from world truth
Lists the clip geometry it assumes (OQ-20 defaults) and what changes if the partner picks differently
The partner is asked to review via an owner:partner issue opened by the sim Manager, linked from the ADR PR

tasks.title: sim: clip renderer v0 and a first labeled clip set
tasks.goal: Implement kitchen/sim/render.py: world runs drawn as abstract RGB frames, passed through the shared change mask and clip builder, and labeled from world truth, so the partner can start training the ConvLSTM.
acceptance: `uv run python -m kitchen.sim.render --seed 7 --count 1000 --out data/clips/v0/` writes npz tensors plus interaction_clip metadata that validate: test_clips_valid
Covers positives (contact with material moved, like a spoon shifting food in a dish), contact without movement, and plain no-contact pairs; label counts reported in a manifest
Uses kitchen/shared/change_mask.py and clips.py only; no local mask or clip code: test_uses_shared_builders
No utensil sprites: the shape set is plain primitives, and a test asserts it (invariant 6)
Same (generator version, seed) gives byte-identical clips: test_render_deterministic
A short README section plus three example clips rendered as GIFs in the PR description (generated files not committed)

tasks.title: sim: hard negatives and domain randomization for clips
tasks.goal: Make it impossible for the ConvLSTM to win by learning that box overlap means transfer: add the hard negatives and randomization from the ADR.
acceptance: Hard negatives, each labeled with labels.hard_negative: overlap_no_contact (one object passes above another), hover, motion_no_contact (nearby stirring), contact_no_motion, camera_noise, lighting_flicker: one unit test each
Randomization of textures, colors, box sizes and aspect ratios, speeds, tracker-like box jitter, missed detections, and dt_ms jitter (15 to 60 FPS equivalents): test_randomization_ranges
A per-hard-negative breakdown in the dataset manifest
Deterministic per seed with all injectors on

tasks.title: sim: ConvLSTM clip dataset with leak-free splits for the partner
tasks.goal: Produce the training dataset the partner uses: large, balanced, with hard negatives at their ADR shares, split so nothing leaks, with a datasheet.
acceptance: `uv run python -m kitchen.sim.clip_data --clips <dir> --out data/clips/<version>/` writes train/val/test with a manifest (counts, label balance, hard-negative shares, sha256, generator version)
At least 50,000 clips; splits by seed range and held-out kitchen layouts; test_no_clip_leakage fails if any seed or layout appears in two splits
A datasheet (markdown, in the PR and in the dataset folder) describing the world, labels, known gaps and how to regenerate
data-manifest.json entry; nothing over 1 MB committed
Handed to the partner on an owner:partner issue opened by the sim Manager
